Maria (CEO): Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands. A few security/privacy follow-ups from folks who couldn't stay — I'm starting this thread so we can capture Qs for leadership.
Daphne (Head of Security): happy to take these. please @mention anything that needs a doc link or an action.
Alex: Quick Q — what is the timeline for SOC2 Type II?
Daphne (Head of Security): Targeting SOC2 Type II for the hosted API by end of Q3. We have the readiness gap list; most work is controls evidence and automation.
Kevin (Eng Lead): Will Dedicated & Private be in scope for the initial Type II?
Daphne (Head of Security): Hosted API will be the initial scope. Dedicated customers with contracts will get independent attestation guidance; Private (VPC/on-prem) is a separate program due to customer-managed infra.
Raj (VP Product): To add — Dedicated customers get enterprise security docs and SOC2-ready configs while we finish audit. We'll offer assessment assistance for Private customers.
Nora (Compliance): Action: Daphne + Nora will publish the SOC2 roadmap doc and the list of mitigation steps by EOD Friday.
Sam: Question — KMS/BYOQ: Are we supporting customer-managed keys for hosted?
Daphne (Head of Security): We have two tracks: 1) KMS integrations for key wrapping (BYOK) in Hosted by mid-Q4. 2) Private installs already support customer KMS/HSM.
Sam: Nice. Any interim options?
Kevin (Eng Lead): For now, we provide envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys and detailed audit logs. If you need BYOK earlier, contact solutions-eng and we can discuss a dedicated contract.
Taylor: Audit log retention — what's the default retention and can customers extend?
Daphne (Head of Security): Default retention for control-plane audit logs is 90 days. Enterprise + Dedicated customers can request extended retention (365d) as an add-on. Private customers control retention in their deployment.
Raj (VP Product): We're also adding log export hooks (S3/BigQuery) so customers can ship logs to their archive. ETA: early next quarter.
Alex: VPC question — will we do VPC peering or private link? Which is recommended?
Kevin (Eng Lead): For Hosted -> customer VPC connectivity we plan to support AWS PrivateLink first. VPC Peering has more networking complexity; PrivateLink is easier to manage and cross-account friendly.
Daphne (Head of Security): Note: PrivateLink will be supported for Dedicated and Private options where networking controls are required. We'll publish architecture examples.
Alex: Any required firewall rules or egress policies to be aware of?
Kevin (Eng Lead): Yes — minimal outbound rules for health checks and metrics. We'll include a simple snippet in the networking guide. e.g.:
```
# allow outbound to redwood-controlplane
10.0.0.0/16 TCP 443
# DNS
0.0.0.0/0 UDP 53
```
Daphne (Head of Security): We won't require broad open access. We'll provide fully-documented whitelists per region.
Jordan: Is ISO 27001 on the roadmap?
Nora (Compliance): Yes — ISO 27001 scoping conversations are underway. We aim to start certification work next fiscal year. No firm dates yet.
Priya: How will audit logs be surfaced in the Console for customers?
Raj (VP Product): Console will show an audit stream (admins only) with filters for user, API key, and route. Download/export planned in the first release.
Daphne (Head of Security): Also delinking: we will have a separate audit log retention policy table in the docs (who can view, how to request exports).
Alex: Will we publish the SOC2 auditor's firm name once selected?
Daphne (Head of Security): Yes — we'll publish the auditor in the roadmap doc once contracts are finalized.
Sam: Follow-up: For BYOK, what KMS providers are targetted? AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault?
Daphne (Head of Security): We're building abstraction for AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS first, then Azure Key Vault. HSM/BYOK for Private installs already flexible.
Kevin (Eng Lead): For engineers — minimal API example (conceptual):
```
POST /v1/keys/wrap
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "key_alias": "projects/x/locations/global/keyRings/r/cryptoKeys/k",
  "plaintext_key": "...base64..."
}
```
Nora (Compliance): Quick note — any BYOK flow will need key rotation docs and customer consent forms in the initial launch. We'll draft templates.
Emma: Are there changes to incident response for Dedicated customers?
Daphne (Head of Security): Yes — Dedicated customers can opt into a faster incident SLA and a dedicated runbook with contact escalation. We'll document differences.
Raj (VP Product): We're also adding per-tenant rate-limit and throttling dashboards to help customers detect anomalous usage.
Maria (CEO): Thanks all. Two asks: 1) publish SOC2 roadmap + auditor once ready; 2) put a short FAQ in the Console — a single-page "security at Redwood" that covers SOC2, KMS, VPC, logs. Daphne + Raj to lead.
Daphne (Head of Security): Acknowledged. We'll post the roadmap in #security-updates and link in Console.
Kevin (Eng Lead): I'll add the networking snippet to the repo and open a PR for the docs.
security-bot: New doc published: /docs/security/soc2-roadmap.md (draft). Link: https://intranet.redwood/docs/security/soc2-roadmap (reaction: :white_check_mark:)
Alex: thanks — please ping when the doc is live, I'll route to my customers.
Daphne (Head of Security): Will do. If anyone else has customer-specific asks, DM me and Nora. :lock:
